home.how_no_shipping: No shipping, no fees through the site.

home.origin_note: Started in Humboldt County, California — now open to anyone, anywhere.
home.why_title: Why this, not the recycling bin
home.why_pp: Deli tubs, yogurt cups and most food containers are polypropylene — recycling code #5. Despite the symbol stamped into the bottom, only 3–8% of it actually gets recycled in practice; most municipal programs don't take it.
home.why_carbon: When recycling does happen, it still costs energy to melt, reprocess and remanufacture — estimates put the carbon savings at 30–80% versus making a container from new plastic. Reusing one as-is skips that process entirely.
home.why_upcycling: Reuse doesn't have to mean the same use. A yogurt tub becomes a seed starter, a big jar becomes a pantry canister, a deli tub becomes the box of screws in someone's garage — what it does next is up to whoever picks it up.
home.why_image_alt: A refrigerator shelf of reused plastic tubs and containers, refilled with leftovers.
home.privacy_pins: A listing's pin marks the neighborhood, never the address. Every location is shifted by a random few hundred metres before it's saved — the exact spot is never stored.
home.privacy_email: Your email address is never shown to anyone, anywhere on the site. Buyers and sellers message each other through the site itself; only your display name is public.
home.privacy_photos: Photos are re-processed before they're stored, which strips the location data most phones quietly attach to pictures.
home.partners_body: Zero-waste groups, repair cafés, community fridges, school and library programs — if keeping usable plastic out of the landfill is already part of what you do, we'd like to hear from you. No ads, no fees, nothing to buy.
home.partners_image_alt: A little free pantry, stocked and labeled "take what you need, give what you can."
